messages.author: cf01a0e462211fab
messages.subject: exogenous (predictor) variable is categorical
parts:
Hi,

I am new to SEM and lavaan so I apologise in advance for probably asking very basic questions. 

I have run a mediation analysis. My predictor variable (Group - controls and brain injury patients) is categorical and I have coded this as a dummy variable (0,1). The mediator (Ability) and outcome (ABASP_GAC - adaptive function) are continuous variables. The code below runs fine but I have a few questions:

1. I am not entirely sure how to interpret the results. For example if my indirect effect is significant does it suggest that the effect of Group on the Outcome is significantly mediated by Ability? i.e. if I have shown that adaptive function is impaired in brain injury patients in comparison to controls (using a t-test) - this effect is mediated by ability?

2. Do I need to run a model that tests the mediation effects in the two groups independently? Or does that just not make any sense because there would be no 'group effect' to mediate? 

model <- ' # direct effect
             ABASP_GAC ~ c*Group
           # mediator (path a)
             Ability ~ a*Group
           # mediator (path b)
             ABASP_GAC ~ b*Ability
           # indirect effect (a*b) 
             ab := a*b
           # total effect
             total := c + (a*b)
         '
I would be very grateful for any advice,
Sara

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: exogenous (predictor) variable is categorical
parts:
1. if my indirect effect is significant does it suggest that the effect of Group on the Outcome is significantly mediated by Ability?

Yes
2. Do I need to run a model that tests the mediation effects in the two groups independently? Or does that just not make any sense because there would be no 'group effect' to mediate?

Right.  In a multigroup model, the effect of the grouping variable would be the difference in intercepts of your mediator (a path) and outcome (c path), and the only regression path explicitly estimated is the b path.  If the b path differs across groups, then the grouping variable is also a moderator (see Preacher et al.'s, 2007, Model 1).

https://doi.org/10.1080/00273170701341316

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts:
Dear Terrence, 

Thank you very much for your help and suggestions. Based on the paper you recommended I thought the following model syntax would make sense:

model1 <- ' # direct effect

ABASP_GAC ~ c*Group
           # mediator (path a)
             Ability ~ a*Group
           # mediator (path b)

ABASP_GAC ~ (b1 + b2*Group)*Ability
           # indirect effect (a*b)
             ab1 := a*b1
             ab2 := a*b2
           # total effect
             total1 := c + (a*b1)
             total2 := c + (a*b2)
'
fit1 <- sem(model1, data = med) 

OR  

fit1 <- sem(model1, data = med, group="Group")

However neither of these estimations run and give me the following error:

Error in lavaanify(model = FLAT, constraints = constraints, varTable = lavdata@ov,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: wrong number of arguments in modifier (b1,b2,Group) of element ABASP_GAC~Ability

I assume there is something wrong with my model (or perhaps completely incorrect) but I cannot identify what this might be. I would be very grateful for your thoughts on the model syntax!

Kind regards,
Sara

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re: exogenous (predictor) variable is categorical
parts:
I don't know if you want to do that (see below). Hopefully I didn't mess up the variable names. If I understand it correctly, you can model Group as an exogenous variable (1) or use a multigroup model (2). In the second case you can check if b is moderated by Group. You can shorten the syntax here and there. Maybe you can see the idea better this way (again: if I don't mix up something). CA

library(lavaan)

# Some meaningless data
set.seed(1234)
Group <- sample(c(0,1), replace=TRUE, size = 1000)
Ability <- Group * 0.5 + sqrt(0.5^2) * rnorm(1000)
ABASP_GAC <- Ability * 0.5 + sqrt(0.5^2) * rnorm(1000)
data <- cbind(Group, Ability, ABASP_GAC)

# (1)
model <- '
Ability ~ a * Group
ABASP_GAC ~ b * Ability + c * Group
ab := a * b
total := ab + c
'

fit <- sem(model, data)
parameterEstimates(fit)

# (2)
model.uncon <- '
Ability ~ c(a1, a2) * 1
ABASP_GAC ~ c(b1, b2) * Ability
ABASP_GAC ~ c(c1, c2) * 1
a := a2 - a1
b := b2
c := c2 - c1
ab := a * b
total := ab + c
'
model.con <- paste(model.uncon, 'b1 == b2')

fit.uncon <- sem(model.uncon, data, group = "Group")
fit.con <- sem(model.con, data, group = "Group")

# Is b moderated by Group?
lavTestLRT(fit.uncon, fit.con)               

parameterEstimates(fit.con)

messages.subject: Re: exogenous (predictor) variable is categorical
parts:
1 to 3: Yes.
4 The model you are using. If the test is not significant, then the constrained model.
5 This is where you got me. I presumed that the models are invariant. Since here b1 == b2, it doesn't matter if you use b := b1 or b:= b2. However, b2 - b1 = 0. If lavTestLRT signals significance, then this would be a special form of moderated mediation. You could then look at Hayes. I think it is the (not uncontroversial) Model 74.
As a supplement, a really ancient but excellent text on means/intercepts in the SEM context can be found here: https://psychology.concordia.ca/fac/kline/Supplemental/means_b.html

parts:
Hi,
Thank you again for the quick reply and useful resources. I will definitely check these out. 

If I have understood the concept of invariance correctly (this assumes that the models for both groups measure the same construct?), I would also assume that the models are invariant due to the fact that the same validated measures are used in both. However, this interpretation may not be correct and I have not formally tested this. My impression is that measurement invariance is usually assessed in multi-group cfa modelling as this formally tests for factors or 'constructs'? 

In addition based on the following paper (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4616155/) I thought the following model might also work (based on their model 8), but was unsure about the difference with the model you proposed.  

modeltest <- '

Ability ~ c(a1, a2) * 1
ABASP_GAC ~ c(b1, b2) * Ability
ABASP_GAC ~ c(c1, c2) * 1

a := a2 - a1

b := b2 - b1
ab1 := a * b1
ab2 := a * b2
intDff := ab2 - ab1
'
The model runs fine and the intDff gives the moderated mediation effect in this case (p-value is in fact the same as through the lavTestLRT). 

Thank you for your help so far, if you have any thoughts on the questions above that would be amazing but I also understand that I can't just keep asking questions!
Sara

On Monday, February 15, 2021 at 1:20:47 PM UTC car...@web.de wrote:
I don't know if you want to do that (see below). Hopefully I didn't mess up the variable names. If I understand it correctly, you can model Group as an exogenous variable (1) or use a multigroup model (2). In the second case you can check if b is moderated by Group. You can shorten the syntax here and there. Maybe you can see the idea better this way (again: if I don't mix up something). CA

library(lavaan)

# Some meaningless data
set.seed(1234)
Group <- sample(c(0,1), replace=TRUE, size = 1000)
Ability <- Group * 0.5 + sqrt(0.5^2) * rnorm(1000)
ABASP_GAC <- Ability * 0.5 + sqrt(0.5^2) * rnorm(1000)
data <- cbind(Group, Ability, ABASP_GAC)

# (1)
model <- '
Ability ~ a * Group
ABASP_GAC ~ b * Ability + c * Group
ab := a * b
total := ab + c
'

fit <- sem(model, data)
parameterEstimates(fit)

# (2)
model.uncon <- '
Ability ~ c(a1, a2) * 1
ABASP_GAC ~ c(b1, b2) * Ability
ABASP_GAC ~ c(c1, c2) * 1
a := a2 - a1
b := b2
c := c2 - c1
ab := a * b
total := ab + c
'
model.con <- paste(model.uncon, 'b1 == b2')

fit.uncon <- sem(model.uncon, data, group = "Group")
fit.con <- sem(model.con, data, group = "Group")

# Is b moderated by Group?
lavTestLRT(fit.uncon, fit.con)               

parameterEstimates(fit.con)

On Saturday, February 13, 2021 at 5:05:36 AM UTC Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
1. if my indirect effect is significant does it suggest that the effect of Group on the Outcome is significantly mediated by Ability?

Yes

2. Do I need to run a model that tests the mediation effects in the two groups independently? Or does that just not make any sense because there would be no 'group effect' to mediate? 

Right.  In a multigroup model, the effect of the grouping variable would be the difference in intercepts of your mediator (a path) and outcome (c path), and the only regression path explicitly estimated is the b path.  If the b path differs across groups, then the grouping variable is also a moderator (see Preacher et al.'s, 2007, Model 1).

https://doi.org/10.1080/00273170701341316
